QUESTION:
What was the default value of `coordinator.batch_size` in PaderQueue 3.x?

DOCUMENTATION EXCERPTS:
[d0103] config | coordinator.batch_size (PaderQueue 3.x) | version 3.x
# `coordinator.batch_size` (PaderQueue 3.x)

> Configuration reference for PaderQueue 3.x.

Number of messages the consumer group coordinator that assigns partitions to consumers processes together in one batch.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Type | integer |
| Default | `500` |
| Available since | 1.2 |
| Component | coordinator |
| Unit | messages |

## Notes

Changes to `coordinator.batch_size` take effect after restarting the node. In clusters, use the same value on all nodes.

Set it in `paderqueue.toml`:

```toml
[coordinator]
batch_size = 500
```

---

[d0211] config | coordinator.batch_size | version 4.x
# `coordinator.batch_size`

> Configuration reference for PaderQueue 4.x (current).

Number of messages the consumer group coordinator that assigns partitions to consumers processes together in one batch.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Type | integer |
| Default | `64` |
| Available since | 1.2 |
| Component | coordinator |
| Unit | messages |
| Default changed | in 4.0 (see release notes) |

## When to change it

The default works for most deployments. Change `coordinator.batch_size` only if you observe problems with the consumer group coordinator that assigns partitions to consumers, for example in the metrics dashboard.

Set it in `paderqueue.toml`:

```toml
[coordinator]
batch_size = 64
```

# `scheduler.batch_size` (PaderQueue 3.x)

> Configuration reference for PaderQueue 3.x.

Number of messages the scheduler that releases delayed messages at their due time processes together in one batch.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Type | integer |
| Default | `100` |
| Available since | 1.1 |
| Component | scheduler |
| Unit | messages |

## Tuning advice

Measure before you tune. Increase or decrease `scheduler.batch_size` in small steps and observe the effect for at least one day.

Set it in `paderqueue.toml`:

```toml
[scheduler]
batch_size = 100
```
